original_value: Multiagent Reinforcement Learning (RL) solves complex tasks that require coordination with other agents through autonomous exploration of the environment. However, learning a complex task from scratch is impractical due to the huge sample complexity of RL algorithms. For this reason, reusing knowledge that can come from previous experience or other agents is indispensable to scale up multiagent RL algorithms. This survey provides a unifying view of the literature on knowledge reuse in multiagent RL. We define a taxonomy of solutions for the general knowledge reuse problem, providing a comprehensive discussion of recent progress on knowledge reuse in Multiagent Systems (MAS) and of techniques for knowledge reuse across agents (that may be actuating in a shared environment or not). We aim at encouraging the community to work towards reusing all the knowledge sources available in a MAS. For that, we provide an in-depth discussion of current lines of research and open questions.

result.paraphrase: Multiagent Reinforcement Learning (RL) addresses complex tasks requiring coordination with other agents through autonomous exploration of the environment. However, training a complex task from scratch is impractical because RL algorithms need enormous amounts of data. For this reason, reusing knowledge from prior experience or other agents is essential for scaling multiagent RL algorithms. This survey offers a unified view of the literature on knowledge reuse in multiagent RL. We present a taxonomy of solutions to the general knowledge reuse problem and provide a comprehensive discussion of recent progress on knowledge reuse in Multiagent Systems (MAS), including techniques for knowledge reuse across agents, whether they act in a shared environment or not. Our goal is to encourage the community to work toward reusing all knowledge sources available in a MAS. To that end, we give an in-depth discussion of current research directions and open questions.
